```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(fastMILC)
library(data.table)
```

`fastMILC` re-implements MILC, the continuous-time microsimulation model of
the natural history of lung cancer (Chrysanthopoulou, 2014). For each person
it simulates the onset of the first malignant cell, tumor growth, the ages at
regional and distant disease, the age, stage and tumor diameter at clinical
diagnosis, and the age and cause of death. Each component is drawn for the
whole population at once:

| Component | Model | Sampler |
|---|---|---|
| Death from other causes | step hazards from the archival cumulative-incidence tables | `nhppp::vdraw_sc_step()` |
| Onset of the first malignant cell | two-stage clonal expansion, piecewise over the smoking history | `nhppp::vdraw_cumulative_intensity()` with a vectorized Newton inverse |
| Progression and stage | Gompertz growth, truncated log-normal volume thresholds | inverse CDF with row-wise rejection |
| Death from lung cancer | step hazards from the archival cumulative-incidence tables | `nhppp::vdraw_sc_step()` |

## Simulating a population

A simulation needs a population recipe, a parameter table and a set of random
number streams. The defaults are the canonical recipe `synthetic_nlst_recipe`
(26,730 synthetic NLST-like current and former smokers aged 49--79 who enter
the study on 2002-06-30) and the baseline parameters `deterministic_params`
(one row per sex).

The random numbers come from named L'Ecuyer streams, one per model component,
held in an `RNGStreams` object. Create it once per session with a seed and
pass it to every simulation:

```{r rng}
rng <- RNGStreams$new(seed = rep(20021115, 6))
```

`Population$new()` draws `target_population_size` people from the recipe rows
with replacement, with probability proportional to the recipe `weight`, and
simulates their histories:

```{r simulate}
p <- Population$new(target_population_size = 5000, rng_stream = rng)
pop <- p$getPopulation()
nrow(pop)
```

The simulation starts at study entry (`spawn_age`). Only people alive and
without a diagnosed lung cancer at entry enter it; a person may have an
undiagnosed malignancy at entry. Each row holds the person's covariates and
parameters and the simulated history:

```{r history}
pop[!is.na(age_at_diagnosis)][1:3, .(
  sex, spawn_age, smoking_status_at_spawn_age,
  age_at_disease_onset, age_at_regional_disease, age_at_distal_disease,
  age_at_diagnosis, stage_at_diagnosis, diameter_at_diagnosis,
  age_dead, cause_of_death
)]
```

Ages are in years. Follow-up ends at death or at the maximum age
`getOption("milc.max_age")` (100); `age_dead` and `cause_of_death` are `NA` for
a person alive at that age. Onset, the stage transitions and diagnosis are
recorded only if they occur before the end of follow-up. The latent ages at
death from each cause are kept in `age_dead_from_other_causes` and
`age_dead_from_lung_cancer`.

## Summarizing the histories

Every simulated history is complete, so cumulative incidence within any
window after entry is a proportion. Diagnoses and deaths within 5, 10 and 20
years of entry:

```{r incidence}
within <- function(t, h) !is.na(t) & t <= h # event within h years of entry
pop[, {
  dx <- age_at_diagnosis - spawn_age
  lung <- fifelse(cause_of_death %in% "lung_cancer", age_dead - spawn_age, NA_real_)
  other <- fifelse(cause_of_death %in% "other_causes", age_dead - spawn_age, NA_real_)
  h <- c(5, 10, 20)
  .(
    years = h,
    diagnosed = sapply(h, function(x) mean(within(dx, x))),
    lung_cancer_deaths = sapply(h, function(x) mean(within(lung, x))),
    other_deaths = sapply(h, function(x) mean(within(other, x)))
  )
}]
```

Stage at diagnosis, over the lifetime:

```{r stage}
pop[!is.na(stage_at_diagnosis), .N, by = stage_at_diagnosis][
  , share := round(N / sum(N), 3)][]
```

## Reproducibility

`Population$new()` resets every stream of `rng` before it simulates, so the
same recipe, parameters and seed give the same population:

```{r reproduce}
p_again <- Population$new(5000, rng_stream = rng)
identical(p_again$getPopulation(), pop)
```

`reset()` removes the simulated columns and `update()` simulates them again
from the start of each component's stream:

```{r reset}
p$reset()
p$update()
identical(p$getPopulation(), pop)
```

## Scenarios

To compare scenarios, change the recipe or the parameters and keep the
streams. Here the tumor growth rate is 20% higher:

```{r scenario}
fast_growth <- copy(deterministic_params)[, tumor_growth_rate := 1.2 * tumor_growth_rate]
pop_fast <- Population$new(5000, parameters = fast_growth, rng_stream = rng)$getPopulation()
rbind(
  baseline = pop[, .(diagnosed = mean(!is.na(age_at_diagnosis)),
                     mean_diameter = mean(diameter_at_diagnosis, na.rm = TRUE),
                     lung_cancer_deaths = mean(cause_of_death %in% "lung_cancer"))],
  faster_growth = pop_fast[, .(diagnosed = mean(!is.na(age_at_diagnosis)),
                               mean_diameter = mean(diameter_at_diagnosis, na.rm = TRUE),
                               lung_cancer_deaths = mean(cause_of_death %in% "lung_cancer"))]
)
```

Both scenarios use the same streams, but the random numbers are not paired
person by person across scenarios: the entry condition redraws different
people when the parameters change.

A recipe is a `data.table` with one row per stratum (here one row per
person), in the format of `synthetic_nlst_recipe`. For example, current
smokers only:

```{r recipe}
current <- synthetic_nlst_recipe[smoking_status_at_spawn_age == "current"]
pop_current <- Population$new(5000, recipe = current, rng_stream = rng)$getPopulation()
pop_current[, .(n = .N, diagnosed = mean(!is.na(age_at_diagnosis)))]
```

`Population$new()` checks the recipe: the required columns, smoking status
(`never`, `former`, `current`) and intensity, and dates of birth, starting and
quitting smoking, and study entry that agree with the status and with each
other.

## Options

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `milc.max_age` | 100 | maximum age; the archival code used 110 (other causes) and 150 (onset) |
| `milc.death_other_tail` | `"archival"` | other-cause death beyond the tabulated window: the archival rule, or `"corrected"` |
| `milc.progression_method` | `"rejection"` | truncated volume thresholds by rejection, or `"conditional"` (three uniforms per person, for common random numbers in calibration) |

## Using a component directly

Each component is a vectorized function. Ages at death from other causes for
three 60-year-old men:

```{r generator}
generate_death_other(
  age_entry = c(60, 60, 60),
  sex = rep("male", 3),
  smoking_status = c("never", "former", "current"),
  intensity = c(0, 20, 20)
)
```

Progression for two people with onset at ages 50 and 60:

```{r progression}
generate_progression(
  age_onset = c(50, 60),
  params = deterministic_params[sex == "male"][c(1, 1)]
)
```

These functions draw from R's current random number generator; inside
`Population` each component uses its own stream.

## Further documentation

The model mathematics, every difference from the archival code, and the
validation against the archival package are in `model_description/model.tex`
in the source repository. The validation harness is in `validation/`.
